key_features.classic_presentation: Ovarian torsion presents with sudden-onset severe unilateral lower abdominal/pelvic pain, often with nausea and vomiting. Pain may be intermittent (torsion/detorsion). More common with ovarian masses (cysts, tumors). Surgical emergency to save ovary.
key_features.typical_demographics: Reproductive age women. Risk factors: ovarian cysts >5cm, ovarian masses, pregnancy.
key_features.pathophysiology_brief: Ovary twists on vascular pedicle causing venous congestion then arterial ischemia and infarction.

diagnostic_questions.context: Sudden onset is classic (70%). May occur during exercise or sudden movement.
Unilateral pain (side of torsion). Right more common than left (3:2 ratio).
Pain is typically severe. May come in waves if intermittent torsion/detorsion.
History of ovarian cyst is major risk factor.

red_flags.action: Time-sensitive - delay causes ovarian loss. Immediate surgical consultation needed.

typical_management: Emergency laparoscopy for detorsion. Goal: save ovary if viable. Delay leads to infarction and ovarian loss.
disposition: Emergency department, immediate OB/GYN surgical consultation.
patient_education: Ovarian torsion is twisting of the ovary cutting off blood supply. It's a surgical emergency to save the ovary. Requires immediate treatment.
